evidence: mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/api/DecimalStringSerializers.kt:46 (DecimalAsLongSerializer.deserialize) does `raw.substringBefore('.').toLong()` and :62 (DecimalAsDoubleSerializer.deserialize) does `raw.toDouble()` on the raw JSON primitive content with NO guard. `toLong()`/`toDouble()` throw NumberFormatException on any non-numeric / empty / unexpectedly-formatted content (e.g. an empty string -> substringBefore('.') = "" -> "".toLong() throws; a null-rendered, grouped, or scientific value throws).

This re-introduces the exact failure mode these serializers were written to eliminate: the file header (lines 20-25) documents issue #2331, where a single fractional monetary field 'silently killed the whole price-tracking payload decode'. An uncaught exception thrown inside kotlinx.serialization deserialize() aborts the entire `response.body()` decode for the favorites/alerts payload (GET /api/v1/favorites, GET /api/v1/favorites/alerts), so one malformed monetary field still sinks every row in the payload — not just that field. Caught at the repo try/catch boundary (becomes Result.failure), so no crash, but the whole screen's data is lost rather than the one bad field degrading gracefully.

Reachability is bounded by the backend (rust_decimal serde-str emits well-formed decimal strings), hence confidence medium / severity low (+1). Fix (KMP-shared, cloud-landable, no backend): wrap the parse (`raw.substringBefore('.').toLongOrNull() ?: 0L` and `raw.toDoubleOrNull() ?: 0.0`, or a try/catch returning a sentinel) so a single malformed monetary value degrades to a default instead of aborting the payload decode, and add a commonTest case feeding a non-numeric string to each serializer.
